task.name: Measure how often a diagnosed fix-success criterion admits a change that removes the symptom without addressing the confirmed cause
task.story_text:
## Why

The fix-success criterion in a diagnosed bug is what a dev is graded against. A criterion
that describes the *absence of the observed symptom* rather than the *presence of the
required property* can be satisfied by a change that suppresses the symptom without
addressing the confirmed cause — and such a change passes review, because review verifies
symptom resolution.

Whether that actually happens is unmeasured. Two facts pull in opposite directions and
neither settles it:

- Forge-diagnosed bugs are the best-performing cohort in the corpus — 6% change-request
  rate against 44% for hand-diagnosed, zero re-runs, $4.71 median cost over 13 sprinted
  issues (measured in #2511). Whatever diagnose is doing with criteria is not obviously
  broken, and intuition-driven edits to its output risk moving it toward the worse cohort.
- The operator-facing doctrine warning against symptom-shaped criteria was written from
  *hand-authored* issues, where the author drafts a criterion immediately after holding
  the mechanism in their head. Diagnose does not work that way, so the doctrine's
  evidence does not transfer, and the doctrine has been applied to diagnose output on
  intuition more than once across controller sessions.

This asks for a rate, not a fix. A null result — the failure mode does not occur often
enough to act on — closes the question, and closing it is worth the measurement, because
the alternative is each session re-deciding by taste whether to hand-edit a diagnosed
body. Sits alongside #2582 and #2586, which exist to decide a policy on evidence rather
than intuition, and is distinct from #2511, which concerns diagnose content that is too
*strong* (unverified repair advice reading as spec) rather than too weak.

## Acceptance criteria

- A report covers a stated set of diagnosed issues over a stated window, naming the
  denominator so the rate can be interpreted, and is reproducible from the audit corpus
  rather than assembled by hand.
- For each issue, the report records whether at least one change existed that would have
  satisfied the recorded fix-success criterion as written while leaving the confirmed
  cause in place, and whether the change that actually landed was such a change.
- The two questions above are reported separately. A criterion that admits a
  symptom-removing change but did not receive one is a different finding from one that
  did, and collapsing them overstates the problem.
- The report states the rate at which the failure mode was realised and records a
  decision: act, or close the question as not occurring at a rate worth acting on.
- Where the failure mode is found, the report names the criteria involved so the pattern
  can be characterised rather than described in the abstract.

## Example

A candidate instance, unadjudicated — the criterion recorded on #2595:

> …completes all N stories without any ESCALATE whose message is the "LANDING
> PRECONDITION: uncommitted changes" string citing `.forge/audits/runs/` or
> `.forge/knowledge/summaries/` paths as the dirt. A precondition refusal caused by
> genuine operator-introduced dirt (unrelated files) must still fire.

Two changes appear to satisfy that text while leaving the cause in place: exempting those
two paths from the project-root dirty check, or writing the artifacts outside the
checkout. Both remove the symptom; neither publishes the corpus, which is what the issue
asks for. Whether either would have survived review is exactly what is unmeasured — the
issue body rules the exemption out in prose, and the dev reads the whole body, so the
criterion being weak in isolation may carry no consequence at all. That is the question.

A report over the diagnosed corpus would classify each criterion this way and produce a
rate, so the answer stops depending on which controller session happens to read a body.

The report's per-issue rows would look like:

| Issue | Criterion admits a symptom-removing change | Landed change was one | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #2595 | yes — path exemption, or relocating the write | no | body rules exemption out in prose |
| #2501 | no | no | criterion names a behavioural property |
| #2191 | yes — named test file passes without cause fixed | unresolved | see #2511 |

Rolled up to two rates over the stated denominator:

```
criteria admitting a symptom-removing change:  N / D
of those, where such a change actually landed: M / N
```

`M / N` is the rate that justifies acting. `N / D` alone does not — a criterion that
could have been gamed but was not is evidence the surrounding body and review are doing
the work, which is itself the finding.

claims.claim: When retaining failed model outputs in append-only audit storage, sidecar filenames must be unique per failure event rather than derived only from issue identity and coarse timestamps, or one failed run can overwrite another's preserved evidence.

Fallback paths that preserve evidence during storage failures need explicit verification, because the only branch exercised in normal operation may hide loss or unbounded persistence behavior until the filesystem refuses the primary write.

Preserving raw failed outputs can create a storage-shape problem of its own: if the retained payload is written verbatim into a JSONL audit stream, a single malformed model response can expand one append-only record arbitrarily.
Operator-visible failure summaries need to expose that raw model output was preserved; otherwise a parse-failure run still appears non-actionable even when the audit layer kept the evidence.

handoff.summary: Built a read-only measurement of how often a diagnosed fix-success criterion admits a change that removes the symptom while leaving the confirmed cause in place, and how often such a change actually landed. Three artifacts: scripts/measure_criterion_gaming.py (stdlib + PyYAML + subprocess git/gh, the scripts/derive_changelog.py pattern, never imports theforge); docs/plans/2603-criterion-symptom-gaming.adjudications.yaml, a checked-in file carrying both the 18 hand-adjudicated judgments and the mechanical facts each was made against; and docs/plans/2603-criterion-symptom-gaming.md, generated from the two and never hand-edited. The mechanical half is derived: diagnose audit YAMLs supply the window, cohort, selected attempt and criterion text, and `git log` over integration refs supplies the landed commit by matching the issue title with the trailing `(#N)` story number stripped. A normal run re-derives every recorded fact and refuses to render on drift, on a missing/extra/unadjudicated row, or on a classification the mechanical join forecloses; it needs neither network nor gh (verified with gh off PATH). Only --refresh-facts writes the file or calls gh. Result over D=18 issues: N/D = 6/18 criteria admitted a symptom-removing change, M/N = 0/6 received one, U=0, decision close.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 treats an exact-title commit returned by git log --all as landed, but --all also traverses preserved feature, backup, and worktree refs. This repository currently retains refs such as feat/issue-2910 and feat/issue-2926, and src/theforge/sprint/launch_guard.py deliberately preserves escalated worktrees. A committed but rejected or unlanded attempt could therefore be classified as the landed change.
  Suggestion: Require a matched commit to be reachable from a designated integration branch, or otherwise record positive landing evidence from a merged carrier; add a fixture where the sole title match exists only on an unmerged feature ref.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The deduplication rule needs the current issue body, but the only specified GitHub query is gh issue view N --json title,state,stateReason, which does not return body. Implemented literally, body-containment selection cannot run.
  Suggestion: Include body in the same gh issue view JSON request and cover its use in the existing dedup fixtures.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] The default window and the adjudication-volume mitigation contradict the corpus. Step 1 sets --since 2026-08-20T00:00:00Z and states in-window phase counts of '23 DONE, 7 FAILED, 2 CAUSE_FOUND_PARTIAL' with a stated risk mitigation of 'D≈20 issues after the cohort rule'. Measured over the operator corpus, those counts belong to the 2026-09-01 window (32 files / 27 issues → 19 after the cohort rule). The plan's actual default window holds 101 diagnose files over 85 issues (77 DONE, 14 FAILED, 8 UNCLASSIFIED_PARTIAL, 2 CAUSE_FOUND_PARTIAL), and after the full cohort rule including the landing.location clause it yields 70 files over 62 issues. The dev following this plan must hand-adjudicate 62 rows — each requiring a git show and a constructed counterfactual change — against a plan that budgets ~20, so the volume risk the plan claims to retire is live and the checked-in report will either blow the budget or be silently truncated. The '16/20 with a unique commit, all 4 misses OPEN' verification was likewise run over the 09-01 cohort plus #2595, not the declared default window.
  Suggestion: Keep the 2026-09-01 lower bound (D=19) and add #2595 by explicit inclusion — e.g. an --include-issue flag or an extra_issues list in the window block — so the spec's worked example is in the denominator without pulling in the 43 additional issues the 08-20 bound admits. Whatever bound is chosen, restate the measured per-clause counts for that exact bound, since the ones in Step 1 belong to a different window.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] The landed-change join calls gh issue view N --json title,state,stateReason per issue at render time, so every re-render of the checked-in report needs network and a working gh auth. gh works from this checkout, but the report is meant to be reproducible from the checked-in facts file, and the Step 1 drift check re-derives mechanical fields on every normal run.
  Suggestion: Record the fetched title and state in the adjudication/facts file during --refresh-facts, and have normal runs drift-check the git-log side only, so a re-render without network still validates and prints. Fail with a named reason rather than an unhandled subprocess error when gh is unavailable.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] The landing.location figures cited for the cohort clause do not match the corpus at the stated window. Among DONE rows with a non-empty criterion since 2026-08-20 there are zero location: null rows (not 23) and 7 dry-run markers (6 <dry-run: body_section> plus 1 <dry-run: comment>, not 8); the 23/8 figures come from the whole corpus including non-DONE attempts. Every other location in-window is of the form issue #N body updated, so no path-shaped pr_to_body location occurs and the indistinguishable_landing bucket is empty in practice.
  Suggestion: Restate the clause counts for the chosen window, and keep the indistinguishable_landing bucket as a defensive zero-count line rather than presenting it as an expected exclusion.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 asserts the fixture-level behaviours but not the end-state property that matters for AC 1: that the D printed in the checked-in report equals the number of adjudication rows and the number of rendered per-issue rows.
  Suggestion: Add one test over the real checked-in adjudication file asserting D == len(issues) == rendered row count, so a truncated adjudication pass fails the gate instead of producing a smaller-than-stated denominator.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 1's window is internally inconsistent with its own measurements, and the error is load-bearing. The plan pins --since 2026-08-20 and claims 'measured in-window: 23 DONE, 7 FAILED, 2 CAUSE_FOUND_PARTIAL' with D≈20; measured against the live corpus, that window actually holds 101 diagnose files over 85 distinct issues with phases 77 DONE / 14 FAILED / 8 UNCLASSIFIED_PARTIAL / 2 CAUSE_FOUND_PARTIAL, and 62 issues survive the plan's cohort rule (the cited counts belong to the 2026-09-01 window: 32 files, 27 issues). Executed as written, Step 2 requires 62 hand-authored adjudication rows — the volume the plan's risk 6 declares intractable — and every calibration claim made 'over the corpus' at cohort size 20 (title join hits 16/20 with unique commits, all 4 misses OPEN, exactly 4 multi-attempt issues, #2909 the sole containment miss) was measured on a cohort that is not the stated window's cohort, so the join hit rate, dedup behavior, and unresolved population for the real 62-issue set are unknown.
  Suggestion: Make the stated window match the measured cohort: either keep since=2026-09-01 (19 survivors, all calibration claims re-measurable at that size) and add an explicit include-list mechanism (--include-issue 2595) so the spec's worked example enters the denominator with its inclusion named in the report, or re-measure every calibration claim (cohort counts, join hit rate, multi-attempt dedup cases, miss states) against the 2026-08-20 window and re-size the adjudication commitment to the real D≈62 explicitly.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 1 says the corpus holds 8 '<dry-run:' landing locations; the live corpus holds 10. The inference rule itself is correct (no dry_run key exists; markers and nulls are the real signals, and the null count of 23 matches).
  Suggestion: Treat the marker counts as estimates; the per-clause exclusion counters Step 3 renders are the authoritative numbers.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] The title join depends on gh issue view for every issue in the denominator, so report regeneration requires network and GitHub auth; a drift-check run (the normal read-only mode) inherits that dependency, which the plan does not state.
  Suggestion: Cache the fetched title/state/stateReason among the mechanical facts written by --refresh-facts so normal drift-checking runs can operate offline, refetching only under --refresh-facts.

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
